name: Pyramid of Cestius
type: pyramid; archaeological site; mausoleum; historical civil building museum; archaeological artifact museum; Italian national museum
text: The pyramid of Cestius (in Italian, Piramide di Caio Cestio or Piramide Cestia) is an ancient Roman pyramid in Rome, Italy, near the Porta San Paolo and the Protestant Cemetery. It was built in the style of the Nubian pyramids as a tomb for Gaius Cestius, a member of the Epulones religious corporation. It stands at a fork between two ancient roads, the Via Ostiensis and another road that ran west to the Tiber along the approximate line of the modern Via Marmorata.

depictions.name: Piramide Cestia
depictions.text: The Pyramid of Cestius (Italian: Piramide Cestia) is a landmark in Rome. In the early 16th century, it concealed the entrance to a Lair of Romulus located within the Catacombs of Rome.
